title: Whole-Body Vibration in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis / Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
summary:
Children and adolescents with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis / Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) often experience severe fatigue and reduced mobility.
This study investigates whether a special vibration-based training device (“Galileo”) can help improve muscle strength and movement abilities.
The training is performed at home in addition to standard care such as physiotherapy, psychotherapy, and pacing.
Researchers will also assess whether the training is safe, practical for families, and whether it enhances overall well-being and quality of life.

interventions.name:
The total study duration is 28 weeks, plus one initial week for baseline assessment.
Participants in Group A start immediately with the Galileo® vibration training, followed by a control phase with standard clinical care only.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed diagnosis of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis / Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)

Age between 6 and 21 years (inclusive)

Bell’s Score > 35, indicating sufficient baseline activity

Written informed consent obtained from the legal guardian and, when applicable, from the participant

Cognitive ability to follow study instructions and training procedures
Exclusion criteria:
No confirmed diagnosis of ME/CFS

Therapy-refractory epilepsy

Severe congenital malformations (e.g. complex congenital heart defect)

Pacemaker or cochlear implant

Thrombosis or endoprosthesis

Recent disc prolapse

Surgically relevant hernia

Botulinum toxin therapy

Fracture, intracerebral hemorrhage, or surgery within the last 3 months

Planned surgery during the study period

Participation in another interventional study

Gallstones or kidney stones in the participant or the assisting person

Pregnancy of the participant or the assisting person

Lack of written informed consent
